clue.text: Happen it will get wasted on unknown nag

parts.note: X is the algebraist's standard unknown quantity

indicators.note: wasted letters are spoilt and squandered, so the words Happen it are rearranged here

explanation.surface: A horse-racing punter laments money squandered on a mystery outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will get wasted' turns HAPPENIT into ANTHIPPE, set after X. 'nag' looks like a horse, but it is the scolding wife of Socrates, whose name became a byword for a shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates' wife was proverbially shrewish, so her name stands for any scolding woman.

clue.text: Ten-nil upset — it's a gas!

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word for nil is read from the bottom up

parts.note: nil means none

explanation.surface: A football fan crows that a ten-nil thrashing was a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's a gas!' reads as slang for great fun, but it literally defines the element; 'upset' turns the word for nil round, giving ENON.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a noble element that exists as a colourless gas at room temperature.

clue.text: Somebody incompetent?

parts.note: split into two words the answer would say a person lacks ability, while as one word it means a celebrity, a somebody

explanation.definitionFit: A somebody is a person of distinction, an eminent public figure.

clue.text: Henry changed Ireland's bad luck

parts.note: H is the symbol of the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the word for the island are put into a new order

parts.note: the possessive 's still gives an S here, so all eight letters are fodder

explanation.surface: A man named Henry reverses the poor fortunes of the Irish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard lines!' is a British expression of sympathy for misfortune; 'changed' gives ARDLINES. Henry is the unit of inductance, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom of commiseration, meaning misfortune or a rotten break.

clue.text: Puppeteer may have to exert influence clandestinely

definitions.meaning: a marionette operator literally tugs on cords to work the figure
to use secret connections behind the scenes to get something done

explanation.definitionFit: Literally the puppeteer's act of tugging cords; figuratively, using hidden contacts and influence.

clue.text: Stage retreat, ignoring the odds

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters of retreat leaves only its second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: An army or theatre company pulls back regardless of the chances against it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage of history is a period or epoch, a distinct span of time.

clue.text: Publication featuring Hardy, for one

definitions.meaning: a magazine of strip cartoons for children
Oliver Hardy, of Laurel and Hardy, was a film comedian

explanation.definitionFit: A strip-cartoon magazine is one sense; a funny performer like Oliver Hardy is the other.

clue.text: Drive carriage? Not I!

indicators.note: Not I says the self, the letter of the first person, is to be refused and dropped

parts.note: a chaise is a light horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: Someone declines an invitation to drive a horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'Not I!'; 'Not' removes I from CHAISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase is to drive away or pursue, as in hunting game.

clue.text: Long-distance traveller wants road to be given subsidy

parts.note: MI stands for the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway
a grant is a sum of money given as a subsidy

explanation.surface: A commuter wants funding for a new motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird or worker that moves seasonally over great distances.

clue.text: Most pleasant stories, after getting me tucked into bed

indicators.note: being tucked into a bed means lying inside it, so these words go inside the word for a small bed

parts.note: a cot is a child's bed

indicators.note: the word for stories follows the word me, as if collected after it

parts.note: lies are false stories

explanation.surface: A child is told the nicest bedtime stories once tucked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into bed' makes the small bed the container, not a picture of a child going to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of an adjective meaning attractive or good-looking.

clue.text: Born out of wedlock, but one sure to succeed

definitions.meaning: an old sense, as in a ... son, illegitimate
someone with innate talent, a born winner

explanation.definitionFit: An old word for an illegitimate child; also a person with innate flair, bound to do well.

clue.text: Alloy with two metals used in a medal

indicators.note: the metals are placed in the abbreviation for a medal, so these go inside it

parts.note: MM is the Military Medal
Al is aluminium
Ga is gallium

explanation.surface: A medal is cast from an alloy of two metals.
explanation.walkthrough: Aluminium and gallium are given by chemical symbols. 'used in a medal' suggests what the medal is made of, but the medal's abbreviation is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A blend of mercury with other metals, as used in dental fillings.

clue.text: "Be acquainted with beauty", said Swedish chemist

indicators.note: said tells us we hear these words spoken, not written

parts.note: be acquainted with is know, and a beauty is a belle

explanation.surface: A Swedish scientist spoke of his wish to meet a beautiful woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, the inventor of dynamite who founded the famous prizes, was a Swedish chemist.

clue.text: Not as well organized as Jackson

indicators.note: organized means put into order, so the words Not as well are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Someone is less well arranged than a person named Jackson.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas 'Stonewall' Jackson was a Confederate general in the American Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of the Confederate general Thomas Jackson, earned for his firmness at Bull Run.

clue.text: Take a trip as soon as unwritten article has been accepted

indicators.note: the phrase for as soon as takes the other words in, holding them inside

parts.note: once means as soon as
verbal means spoken, not written
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A traveller sets off on a journey once a spoken agreement is made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take a trip' means to fall over, not to travel; 'unwritten' is spoken, as in a verbal agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose one's balance and topple, as a stumble does.

clue.text: Nothing splits up partnership, that's the trouble

indicators.note: the round letter splits the pair, standing between its two letters

parts.note: we denotes a couple or partnership
O is the zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A couple's problem is that they have nothing, so they separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief or affliction, misery.

clue.text: Having got exhausted, scratched

parts.note: with means having, as in a man with a hat
drawn means haggard, worn out

explanation.surface: A runner, worn out, pulls out of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratched' is the racing sense: taken out of the event.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor pulled from a race is said to be scratched.

clue.text: Scripture held in varying reverence as a source of control

indicators.note: the scripture letters are held inside the rearranged word
varying shows the letters of reverence are altered into a new order

parts.note: NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: Holy writ is regarded with differing degrees of awe as a guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varying' rearranges the letters into NERVECERE; New Testament is the usual scripture abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A hub or headquarters from which an organisation is directed, like the body's nerve hub.

clue.text: English instructor depresses a number of voters

indicators.note: in a down clue the instructor sits on top of what follows, pressing it down

parts.note: a lector is a university lecturer
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: An English teacher dispirits some voters.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relating to an electorate, the body of people who vote.

clue.text: Unfaithful just after tea, say

indicators.note: the word for just comes after the letter from tea
say shows the drink's name is spoken, giving the letter of the same sound

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like T
just means fair, reasonable

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of infidelity just after tea time.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasonable acts betray one's country, being disloyal.

clue.text: Catch up 5 points

parts.note: ... compass points

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the answer to 5 is turned round

parts.note: the answer to 5 Down is the word for an epoch

explanation.surface: Someone catches up five points in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the answer to 5 Down round, giving ARE; the four compass points are a crossword staple for letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To trap or snare.

clue.text: Some have to be critical examiners

indicators.note: some says only part of the words have to is taken

explanation.surface: Some people must be harsh judges.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrutinise carefully, checking thoroughly.

clue.text: Luxurious residence, home for criminal

parts.note: a villa is a large luxurious house
in means at home

explanation.surface: A grand house serves as a crook's hideout.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer, scoundrel or lawbreaker.

clue.text: Notice girl's prayer-book

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so girl's is Di's
a missal is a book of Mass prayers

explanation.surface: A girl's prayer book is noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Notice as in being given one's notice, sacked from a job.

clue.text: Plant with green leaves, variegated with gold and cream

indicators.note: a variegated plant is mixed with another colour, so the gold letters go inside

parts.note: ivy is an evergreen climbing plant
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a plant with leaves mottled gold and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-white colour, like elephant tusks.

clue.text: Bulb could be lit up

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters of lit up can make another word

explanation.surface: A light bulb could be switched on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' looks like a lamp, but it is a flower's bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring flower grown from a bulb.

clue.text: Man still spoken of

indicators.note: spoken of shows the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: still as a noun means quiet, calm

explanation.surface: A man who is still talked about.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess or draughts, a man is any playing unit.

clue.text: Sailor, a solitary inhabitant of the deep

parts.note: AB is able seaman
lone means solitary

explanation.surface: A lone sailor lives at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A shellfish, an edible sea snail.

clue.text: Mischievous creature in the money? Penniless, in fact

indicators.note: penniless says the letter for a penny is removed

parts.note: pelf is money, wealth

explanation.surface: A mischievous creature rich at first is actually broke.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mischievous fairy.

clue.text: Tell island about Lawrence, initially

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the island name runs backwards

parts.note: Arran is a Scottish island
T E are the initials of T E Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: Someone recounts an island story about Lawrence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ARRAN into NARRA. 'initially' signals T.E. Lawrence's initials, not just the first letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate or recount a story.

clue.text: Poor Edward imprisoned by marshal

indicators.note: being imprisoned by means held inside, so the short name goes inside the marshal

parts.note: Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Poor Edward is jailed by a military officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking money, poverty-stricken.

clue.text: Republic harbours chap who's evasive and mercenary

indicators.note: harbours means shelters within, so the evasive chap goes inside the republic

parts.note: France is a republic
an eel is a slippery, evasive person

explanation.surface: A republic shelters an elusive soldier for hire.
explanation.walkthrough: Originally a hired medieval knight, the answer means a soldier for hire.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone selling services for pay, like a hired soldier.
